title: Choose the visual world for azure-lupa
question: The roll assigned Concourse Signage. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. Layout, navigation and controls stay standard in every option; the world lends type, palette, density and one signature move.

options.label: Concourse Signage
options.lineage: Airport wayfinding programs (Schiphol, Kinneir/Calvert, Frutiger at Charles de Gaulle)
options.thesis: A sprawling estate made walkable: every resource type gets a concourse zone colour and pictogram, and where you are is always stated on a yellow directional sign.
options.viewport: Dark charcoal rail on the left holds the tenant → subscription → resource-group tree. Across the top of the work area a yellow sign band reads the current location as a directional sign (Tenant › Subscription › RG ›) with the search field set into it. Below: a dense resources table on a pale ground; each row leads with a small square zone tile (Compute blue, Network teal, Storage rust, Data violet) carrying the type pictogram. Right drawer opens details.
options.risk: Zone colours must be curated to ~8 categories; unmapped types fall back to neutral grey, and yellow on a light ground needs a dark text plate to pass contrast.

raised.raise: IDs, counts and timestamps are set in tabular monospace at full density; no grey decoration anywhere, only data and signs.
The table uses one type size; rank is carried by weight, case and the zone tile, never by size.
Every row deep-links to its position in the tree: selecting a resource lights its subscription and RG in the rail.
The yellow appears only where you are or what you can act on; it never decorates.

options.label: Survey Sheet
options.lineage: Ordnance Survey / USGS topographic map sheets
options.thesis: The estate as surveyed terrain: subscriptions are map sheets, locations are grid squares, and every resource has a grid reference.
options.viewport: Magenta header strip like a map cover with the sheet title (subscription). Left: tree. Main: table with a legend-key glyph per type column; a thin index-map strip above shows resource density per region as tinted grid squares, clickable as a location filter.
options.risk: Cartography is the most familiar 'inventory' metaphor; the region grid only earns its place if location filtering is frequent.

options.label: Datamatics Field
options.thesis: Pure black and white data density: the inventory as a field of tabular numerics with a barcode strip of resource counts.
options.viewport: Black ground, white monospace table edge to edge; a hairline barcode strip above encodes counts per type, selecting a bar inverts its rows.
options.case: Holds product clarity (density, scan speed) but loses audience identification: engineers read it as art, not a tool; no colour for state.
options.risk: Without colour, errors and needs-login states depend on inversion alone.

options.label: Timetable Slide Rack
options.lineage: 1971 pocket airline timetable on a light table
options.case: Raked containers and lateral travel fight a fast-scanning table; loses both axes.
options.kept: One type size in the table; rank by weight and case.

options.label: Convention Circle Catalog
options.case: Resources have no thumbnails; a stamp grid hides names and types.

options.label: Crouwel Grid Specimen
options.case: Monumental type wastes the density engineers need; loses both axes.

options.label: Warm Consumer Surface
options.case: Touch-first single column is wrong for a desktop data tool.
options.kept: Accent reserved strictly for actionable elements.

options.label: Cassette J-card
options.case: Hand-lettering undermines trust in exact IDs; loses both axes.
options.kept: Running totals right-aligned tight to the margin.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: Azure Portal / Linear-style data app executed cleanly: neutral greys, one blue accent.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar tree, toolbar with search and filter chips, data table, details sheet.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other admin tool by design.
